title: Tier0 — A100 kernel baseline (throughput envelope, per-gen, parity, scale)
question: Re-establish the kernel's core numbers on the real target hardware (8x A100-80GB): throughput vs batch size for all 3 variants, EvoGP per-gen wallclock (the CO-fraction denominator), fp32-vs-fp64 parity, and the magnitude-scan quality gate. fp32 throughout.
setup: Single A100 per timed run, manually pinned (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES), pool GPU2-7 (left 0,1 for the box owner's jobs). Throughput swept on one synthetic preset (early-gen) varying M, so per-tree cost is fixed and the curve isolates GPU-utilization scaling. N=7 timed repeats + 2 warmup discarded; device wall-time parsed from the binary. Clocks unlocked (no sudo) but boost to the 1410 MHz SM ceiling under sustained load.

env.clock_policy: UNLOCKED (no sudo); SM auto-boosts to 1410 MHz under load, sampled per-run
env.exclusivity: manual pin + pre-check; pool GPU2-7 verified free at launch

sweep.variants: batch_lm (baseline, host-FD), batch_lm_devjac (device Jacobian), batch_lm_fusedfd (fused FD)
sweep.M_list: 1000, 4000, 16000, 64000 (+256000 for devjac/fusedfd; baseline stops at 64k: host-FD too slow + saturated)
sweep.metric: trees/s = M / device_wall_time; report median + p10/p90
sweep.reference_point: real data/fixtures/pop.bin (1000 real EvoGP trees) kept for cross-machine (laptop) comparison

kernel.precision: fp32 (design target: EvoGP + pop.bin data are fp32; no fp64 signal to recover)
kernel.timing_source: clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) around the full solve (device wall, host orchestration included)

synth_gen.early-gen_marginals: mirrors real snapshot I.18.12_pop4000 gen5: nodes_mean 12.4, K_mean 2.77, trig 0.30 (calibrated to within +/-5%)
synth_gen.tree_structure: size ~ lognormal(2.40,0.54) clipped 3-32 nodes; ops weighted by real opcode frequencies; leaves var/const by p_const
synth_gen.c_init: c_true * U(0.7,1.3) + N(0,0.02)  (constants perturbed ~+/-30%, mimics 'not yet tuned')
synth_gen.x_points: U(0.5,2.5), shared across the whole population
synth_gen.rejection: resample trees whose y is non-finite or |y| > 1e6 (DIV poles, tan asymptotes)
synth_gen.problem_type: RECOVERABLE (CO can reach near c_true) -> performance + precision axis (NOT the quality-tier story)

findings.evidence: baseline @ M=1000 = 787 t/s, BELOW the laptop 5070Ti's 1319 t/s. The big GPU is latency/overhead-bound at this batch -> a fixed 1000-tree throughput is meaningless on A100; you must sweep M.

findings.claim: The variant gap WIDENS at scale on A100 (opposite of the laptop-PCIe hypothesis)
findings.evidence: At M=64k fusedfd 36551 vs baseline 1277 t/s (~29x); fusedfd reaches 50394 @256k still climbing. baseline's host-FD does H<->D round-trips every FD step -> a serial bottleneck that does NOT scale with the GPU, while devjac/fusedfd stay on-device. RERUN_A100.md predicted the gap would NARROW on A100; it widens.

findings.claim: fusedfd has not saturated even at 256k; devjac plateaus ~24k; baseline flat ~1.3-1.5k
CO remains the absolute bottleneck of the GP loop
findings.evidence: EvoGP per-gen evolution = 5.2ms (pop1000) / 5.3ms (pop4000) mean, while one full-population CO pass is hundreds of ms -> in-loop time is dominated by CO.

findings.claim: fp32 quality is unchanged on A100 vs laptop
findings.evidence: parity gate 3/3 PASS at 94.0 / 92.4 / 99.8 (loss-down / within-1.05x / within-10x), identical to the laptop baseline; magnitude scan tier1 11/11 + tier2 5/5 PASS for all 3 variants.

findings.claim: Unlocked clocks are stable for timing
findings.evidence: SM clock sampled at 1410 MHz (the A100 ceiling) across all sustained-load timed runs; no sudo needed to lock.

tables.name: Parity gate (A100, fp32 vs scipy fp64)

plots.caption: CO throughput vs batch size M (log-log, fp32, N=7 median +/- range). x markers = laptop 5070Ti @ M=1000 reference. Wide-M points (64k-256k) are saturation/envelope probes, not a realistic-workload claim.

caveats: Synth = recoverable problem (performance + precision axis). Real GP snapshots (the quality-tier story) are a separate run, not included here.
The first sweep was DISCARDED: un-killed duplicate (pre-fix) processes co-tenanted GPU2-4 and contaminated timing + raced the output files. Numbers here are the clean single-process rerun (tp2_*).
baseline @ 256k skipped: host-FD ~160s/run x 9 is wasteful and it is already saturated by 4k.
M up to 256k is a saturation/envelope probe; the 'realistic operating point' is co-designed with kernel performance and decided later (not pinned to today's pop=4000).
Clocks unlocked (no sudo); they boost to 1410 MHz under load and are recorded per run, but not hard-pinned.
reproduce: cd cusr/kernel && nvcc -O2 -arch=sm_80 -std=c++17 -lineinfo --use_fast_math -o batch_lm_devjac batch_lm_devjac.cu loader.c && cd ../..
# throughput sweep (one variant per pinned GPU): python sweep.py --bin <bin> --gpu <id> --label <v> --out <f> --mlist 1000,4000,16000,64000,256000
# parity: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<g> GATE_REPORT=docs/kernel/verify_report_a100.md uv run python cusr/kernel/tests/test_parity_gate.py
# scale: BATCH_LM=cusr/kernel/batch_lm_<v> uv run python cusr/kernel/tests/test_fixture_scale.py
